name: Beinn Odhar Foothill Ascent
notes: Gentle opening climb departing Tyndrum on firm stony track with expansive views north into the Breadalbane Hills.

name: Gleann Meran Pass
notes: Ascends the Auch Estate into Gleann Meran beneath soaring Munro ridges before dropping towards Glen Lyon.

name: Rannoch Divide Moorland Ascent
notes: A stiff climb up the Glen Lyon road pass crossing exposed peat moors towards Kinloch Rannoch.

name: Dunan Moor Crossing
notes: Traverses undulating estate gravel through ancient Caledonian pine remnants.

name: Loch Ericht Headwaters Ascent
notes: Enters wild remote country along the western shoreline approaches to Ben Alder Cottage.

name: Bealach Dubh (Ben Alder Pass)
notes: Rough, high mountain pass climbing to 669m through an amphitheatre of scree between Ben Alder and Beinn Bheoil.

name: Corrieyairack Pass Summit
notes: The iconic crown of the Highland Trail 550. An 18th-century military road climbing through 13 hairpin switchbacks to the route's highest altitude at 769m (2,522 ft).

name: Great Glen Northern Ridge
notes: Sustained 9-mile forestry ascent out of Fort Augustus gaining 468m with dramatic vistas back over Loch Ness.

name: Strathglass Forest Climb
notes: Fast rolling forestry gravel through deep pine woodlands.

name: Strathconon Divide
notes: Steep unpaved climb over the watershed between Glen Orrin and Strathconon.

name: Torrachilty Forest Crest
notes: Woodland singletrack and fire road climb arriving into Contin resupply.

name: Strath Vaich High Pass
notes: Remote estate doubletrack gaining 191m into the lonely glens of central Ross-shire.

name: Glenbeg Stalker Crossing
notes: Exposed moorland doubletrack connecting Strath Rannoch to the upper Carron drainage.

name: Bealach na h-Uidhe (Sutherland Plateau)
notes: Long gradual 9-mile haul ascending the Sutherland wilderness plateau onto lonely heather moors.

name: Loch Merkland Divide
notes: Short, punchy climb transitioning over the divide between Loch Shin and the northern sea lochs.

name: Strath More / Foinaven Ascent
notes: Rugged singletrack climb into the dramatic quartzite shadow of Foinaven in the far northwest Highlands.

name: Bealach nam Fiann (Far North Ridge)
notes: Brutal 271m rocky ascent over 1.4 miles (12% grade) requiring technical hike-a-bike over loose quartzite boulders.

name: Bealach a' Chraisg (Kylesku Pass)
notes: Spectacular technical descent and climb linking sea lochs Glencoul and Glendhu with soaring views of Quinag.

name: Loch na Gainmhich Crest
notes: Rolls over coastal gneiss knolls past Britain's highest waterfall overlook.

name: Loch Broom Overlook
notes: Punchy scenic climb cresting above Ullapool harbour and ferry terminal.

name: Rhidorroch Moor Climb
notes: Ascends east from Ullapool along the river before climbing into remote high heather moors.

name: Sail Mhor Pass (Gateway to Fisherfield)
notes: Steep rocky trail climbing 345m out of Dundonnell straight into the heart of the Great Wilderness under An Teallach.

name: Bealach na Croise (Fisherfield Pass)
notes: The legendary Fisherfield test. River crossings, peat hags, and a fierce 438m ascent through Britain's most isolated wilderness.

name: Kernsary Forest Ascent
notes: Rolling forest track linking the remote sands of Poolewe with the western shores of Loch Maree.

name: Bealach na Lice (Torridon Pass)
notes: World-class mountain biking singletrack. Climbs through massive Torridonian sandstone slabs into Coire Lair beneath Beinn Damh.

name: Coulin Forest Pass
notes: Technical descent and climb over ancient Torridon gneiss into Strathcarron.

name: Loch Carron Overlook
notes: Rises over the coastal ridge towards the iconic silhouette of Eilean Donan Castle.

name: Bealach an Sgairne (Kintail Divide)
notes: Sustained 344m climb up Glen Lichd beneath the near-vertical walls of the Five Sisters of Kintail.

name: Glen Affric High Saddle
notes: Wild mountain saddle crossing the watershed into the Caledonian pine forests of Glen Affric.

name: Gleann Lichd / Camban Pass
notes: Epic 450m backcountry ascent passing Camban Bothy into one of Scotland's most celebrated wild glens.

name: Glen Moriston South Ridge
notes: Forestry spine climb linking Glen Moriston to Loch Garry and the Great Glen Way.

name: Lairig Leacach Ascent
notes: Traverses the dramatic pass between the Grey Corries and the Mamores towards Fort William.

name: Glen Nevis Foothills
notes: Climbs the southern shoulders of Glen Nevis out of Fort William with views of Britain's highest peak.

name: Devil's Staircase Ascent
notes: The famous Devil's Staircase out of Kinlochleven: a relentless 526m climb over 5.3 miles across switchbacks to the Glencoe high pass (549m).

name: Rannoch Moor Drovers Crest
notes: Crosses the legendary peat expanse of Rannoch Moor along the Telford parliamentary road towards Bridge of Orchy.

name: Auchtertyre Final Crest
notes: The final climb of the Highland Trail 550! Crests the shoulder of Strath Fillan before rolling triumphantly into Tyndrum finish.
